items.statement: Nonmonotonic static HRS response under structural extension
items.expected: Use the actual comparable static isotropic beta_HRS responses of complete gas-phase neutral-singlet helicenes 1, 3, 5 and 7 to establish that extension 1→5 increases the response whereas 5→7 decreases it. Quantify the signed changes and substantiate their resolution using the response tensors and the declared derivative, orientation-average and unit conventions. This establishes a nonmonotonic physical size/extension relationship, not four successful scalar calculations or a pair of unexplained signs. beta_total, a selected Cartesian component, finite-frequency response or copied source magnitudes cannot establish this result. The source HRS magnitudes are comparison evidence, with no matching windows.

A quantitative comparison derives from actual comparable response values that the absolute3-versus7 HRS difference is smaller than both the1-to5 increase and the5-to7 decrease, and therefore identifies3/7 as similar-magnitude responses despite different full structures. It must show these relative contrasts and account for numerical resolution before asserting a fine3/7 ordering; merely listing limits earns zero. Physical comparison: Complete gas-phase neutral-singlet helicenes 1/3/5/7 (48/56/72/76 atoms), static omega=0. Source baseline is B3LYP/6-31G(d) ground-state geometries followed by CAM-B3LYP/6-31+G(d) response. HRS is the rotationally averaged tensor invariant in main Eqs15–18, not beta_total. Physically comparable alternative methods are permitted.

items.statement: Dipolar and octupolar character across the four responses
items.expected: Establish the physical character of each actual static response and the contrast across all four helicenes: 1 is dipolar-dominated, 3 and 7 are strongly octupolar-dominated, and 5 is dipolar-dominated with a substantial octupolar contribution in the supported reference description. Use calculated tensor, polarization or an equivalent physically justified decomposition with defined rotation/derivative conventions. The conclusion is the comparison of molecular response character, not completion of DR, J1/J3 or rho analyses; no specific descriptor, exact ratio, software or author tensor representation is mandatory. Supported equivalent decompositions pass. Shape names or beta_HRS magnitudes alone do not determine response character.

items.statement: What the molecular comparison establishes about structure and response
items.expected: Give an evidence-based physical interpretation of why response magnitude is not determined by carbon count alone: connect the actual molecular structural differences to changes in response anisotropy and the balance of irreducible dipolar/octupolar response. State what the computed tensor and structural evidence distinguishes and whether it isolates a unique causal geometry or charge-transfer descriptor. The added conclusion is the physically justified attribution and its limitations; repeating the scalar ordering or tensor class already scored elsewhere does not pass. No prescribed torsion intervention, density metric, minimum count or exclusive charge-transfer mechanism is required. Well-supported equivalent explanations pass; the four-molecule gas/static comparison cannot by itself establish bulk performance or universal behavior of all pi extensions.
